modelResponse.episodeSummary: 28-year-old male with sudden onset of irregular tachycardia and hemodynamic compromise (BP 82/48) during physical exertion.
keyECGEvidence: morphology: Beat-to-beat QRS width and morphology variation; delta waves visible in wider beats
modelResponse.mechanism: Pre-excitation of the ventricles via an accessory pathway (delta waves) combined with rapid atrial fibrillation, leading to a high-rate, irregularly irregular ventricular response and acute hemodynamic instability.
contributingFactors: Physical exertion (basketball) triggering rapid heart rate
Acute hemodynamic compromise (BP 82/48, MAP 59) due to tachycardia-induced reduced stroke volume
History of self-terminating rapid heart rate episodes

rejectedAlternatives.why: Rhythm is 'irregularly irregular' and morphology shows delta waves; VT is typically regular.
Rhythm is irregularly irregular and lacks consistent P-wave morphology; high likelihood of AFib with pre-excitation.

recommendedActions: Establish large-bore IV access and initiate fluid resuscitation
Avoid AV-node blocking agents (e.g., Beta-blockers, Calcium Channel Blockers, Adenosine) as they may accelerate conduction through the accessory pathway
uncertainty: Lack of prior ECG makes definitive diagnosis of WPW syndrome based on baseline morphology impossible, but clinical presentation and delta waves are highly suggestive.
SpO2_pct: 92 is slightly low but may be secondary to poor perfusion or respiratory rate of 26.
